arxiv-1403-6110.creator: T. Machida 1 , Y. Fujisawa 1 , M. Nagao 2,3 , S. Demura 3 , K. Deguchi 3 , Y. Takano 3 and H. Sakata 1
arxiv-1403-6110.description: A 2014 arXiv research paper by T. Machida 1 , Y. Fujisawa 1 , M. Nagao 2,3 , S. Demura 3 , K. Deguchi 3 , Y. Takano 3 and H. Sakata 1. We present scanning tunneling microscopy measurements on a cleaved surface of the recently discovered superconductor NdO 0.7 F 0.3 BiS 2 with a transition temperature ( T c T_{\mathrm{c}} ) of 5.1 K.

arxiv-2101-08699.title: An empirical evaluation of active inference in multi-armed bandits
arxiv-2101-08699.creator: Dimitrije Marković, Hrvoje Stojić, Sarah Schwöbel, Stefan J. Kiebel
arxiv-2101-08699.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Dimitrije Marković, Hrvoje Stojić, Sarah Schwöbel, Stefan J. Kiebel. A key feature of sequential decision making under uncertainty is a need to balance between exploiting–choosing the best action according to the current knowledge, and exploring–obtaining information about values of other actions. The multi-armed bandit problem, a classical task that captures this trade-off, served as a vehicle in machine learning for developing bandit algorithms that proved to be useful in numerous industrial applications.

arxiv-2409-06436.creator: Simon Flury, Wolfgang J. Simeth, Danielle R. Yahne, Daniel G. Mazzone, Eric D. Bauer, Priscila F. S. Rosa, Romain Sibille, Oksana Zaharko, Dariusz J. Gawryluk, Marc Janoschek
arxiv-2409-06436.description: Abstract The tetragonal 4 ​ f 4f -electron intermetallic ErB 4 is characterized by strong Ising anisotropy along the tetragonal c c axis. The magnetic moments on the erbium sites can be mapped onto a Shastry-Sutherland (SSL) lattice resulting in geometrical frustration. At zero magnetic field ErB 4 exhibits collinear columnar antiferromagnetic (CAFM) order below T N = 15.4 T_{\text{N}}=15.

arxiv-2411-14511.title: Variational Autoencoders for Efficient Simulation-Based Inference
arxiv-2411-14511.creator: Mayank Nautiyal, Andrey Shternshis, Andreas Hellander, Prashant Singh
arxiv-2411-14511.description: Abstract We present a generative modeling approach based on the variational inference framework for likelihood-free simulation-based inference. The method leverages latent variables within variational autoencoders to efficiently estimate complex posterior distributions arising from stochastic simulations. We explore two variations of this approach distinguished by their treatment of the prior distribution.

arxiv-2506-02311.title: Unicorn-CIM: U nconvering the Vul n erability and I mproving the Resilien c e o f High-P r ecisio n C ompute- i n- M emory
arxiv-2506-02311.creator: Qiufeng Li, Yiwen Liang, Weidong Cao
arxiv-2506-02311.description: Abstract Compute-in-memory (CIM) architecture has been widely explored to address the von Neumann bottleneck in accelerating deep neural networks (DNNs). However, its reliability remains largely understudied, particularly in the emerging domain of floating-point (FP) CIM, which is crucial for speeding up high-precision inference and on-device training.

arxiv-2508-12499.title: A Ramsey Ion Gradiometer for Single-Molecule State Detection
arxiv-2508-12499.creator: Sean D. Huver
arxiv-2508-12499.description: Abstract The characterization of ligand–receptor interactions is a cornerstone of modern pharmacology; however, current methods are hampered by limitations such as ensemble averaging and invasive labeling. We propose a theoretical quantum sensing solution, the Quantum Ligand-Binding Interrogator (QLI), designed to overcome these challenges.

arxiv-2511-08595.title: Chopping Trees: Semantic Similarity Based Dynamic Pruning for Tree-of-Thought Reasoning
arxiv-2511-08595.creator: Joongho Kim, Xirui Huang, Zarreen Reza, Gabriel Grand, Kevin Zhu, Ryan Lagasse
arxiv-2511-08595.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Joongho Kim, Xirui Huang, Zarreen Reza, Gabriel Grand, Kevin Zhu, Ryan Lagasse. Tree-of-Thought (ToT) reasoning boosts the problem-solving abilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) but is computationally expensive due to semantic redundancy , where distinct branches explore equivalent reasoning paths. We introduce Semantic Similarity-Based Dynamic Pruning (SSDP) , a lightweight method that, to the best of our knowledge, is the first framework to integrate online semantic merging into parallelized tree search, enabling the clustering and pruning of redundant steps in real time.
